content:
natalie: Heads up — someone reported our SDK breaks on Vercel Edge with `TypeError: require is not defined` after upgrading to v2, plus TS overload inference is messy.
ishaan: Likely ESM/CJS mismatch. Do they have `type: "module"` and still use `require()` in samples?
caroline: Yep. Their package.json is ESM but a leftover example uses `const { createClient } = require('redwood-inference')`. Edge throws.
ryan: We should ship a clear ESM entry and keep a CJS entry in `exports`. Example: "exports": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js"}.
natalie: Also TS errors: `No overload matches this call` when calling `createClient()` with no args. Our overloads are too strict.
ishaan: Simple fix: add permissive signature `createClient<T = any>(opts?: ClientOptions & { model?: T }): Client<T>` so default inference works.
caroline: For `unknown` vs `any` — internal libs can use `unknown`, but exported types should include ergonomic aliases: `type SDKResponse<T = any> = ResponseShape<T>`.
ryan: Edge runtime notes: avoid top-level `process.env` usages, Buffer, and sync fs in examples. Use `globalThis` guards.
natalie: Add a tiny Vercel Edge sample under examples/edge-minimal with `package.json` `type: module` + minimal tsconfig snippet.
ishaan: Recommend tsconfig in README: `module: ESNext`, `moduleResolution: bundler`, `target: ES2020`.
caroline: CI action: matrix of TS versions + common tsconfigs to catch regressions. Also lint rule to fail on `require(` in edge examples.
natalie: I'll draft a PR that: 1) adds permissive overloads, 2) exports `SDKResponse<T = any>`, 3) adds edge example + README snippet.
devex-bot: Created issue #3341: "dx: TS overload ergonomics + ESM/CJS Edge guidance" and linked this thread.
